initial_expert_decisions.location: Discussion, paragraph 1; see also Introduction and Methods
initial_expert_decisions.quote: Moreover, the poor phonological decoders with DD not only demonstrated less sensitivity to the FD illusion compared to the typical reading age- and IQ-matched group (supporting Pammer and Wheatley, 2001 ), but also to a reading-level and IQ-matched control group. The latter result excludes that the M-D deficit is simply an effect of DD. This is the first study to show that the M-D deficit in children with DD is present also when compared with younger children with the same reading performance, challenging the idea that the M-D deficit is a simple effect of reading deprivation and not a cause, as recently suggested by Olulade et al. (2013) .
initial_expert_decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent (never previously adjudicated). The candidate target Olulade, Napoliello, & Eden (2013, 'Abnormal visual motion processing is not a cause of dyslexia', Neuron, doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2013.05.002) is positively established as background/theoretical context rather than an empirically retested target study, whereas the actual empirical target is already represented by shipped input_row_index 697 (Pammer & Wheatley, 2001, 'Isolating the M(y)-cell response in dyslexia using the spatial frequency doubling illusion', doi:10.1016/s0042-6989(01)00092-x; sibling target_index 0). In the Introduction and Methods, the authors explicitly adopt the spatial frequency-doubling (FD) perimetry task and settings of Pammer and Wheatley (2001) to test magnocellular-dorsal (M-D) sensitivity in Italian dyslexic children with poor phonological decoding versus chronological-age controls (Experiment 1), and then conduct an internal replication of Experiment 1 in a new group of poor phonological decoders while extending the FD illusion paradigm to include a reading-level (RL) control group (Experiment 2, motivated in the Introduction by citing Goswami, 2003, noting that 'The RL children (see Goswami, 2003 ) were never included in previous studies using FD illusion'). Olulade et al. (2013) is never mentioned in Methods or Results, appears in the Introduction only in parenthetical '(e.g., ...)' background lists of controversy/noise-exclusion accounts, and is cited once in the Discussion as a general causal interpretation ('the idea that the M-D deficit is a simple effect of reading deprivation and not a cause, as recently suggested by Olulade et al. (2013)') challenged by the novel RL extension. A fresh literal quote preserving the exact source spacing before the final period is provided.

initial_expert_decisions.quote:
First, we did not investigate whether generating and comparing keywords not only enhances judgment accuracy but also promotes learning via regulation. Although this link between enhanced judgment accuracy, regulation, and learning is intuitively plausible and assumed by theories of self-regulated learning (e.g., Nelson and Narens
1994
; Zimmerman
2008
) as well as by empirical studies (e.g., De Bruin et al.
2011
; Thiede et al.
2003
; Rawson et al.
2011
), we did not focus on this aspect in the present study.
initial_expert_decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work (and Luna's mechanical quote error was caused by stripping newline characters from the source text). In the full text, the authors conduct a single conceptual replication test of the delayed-keyword effect on relative metacomprehension accuracy in university students without restudy/regulation, which is already represented by shipped row 139 (Thiede; Dunlosky; Griffin; Wiley, 2005, 'Understanding the Delayed-Keyword Effect on Metacomprehension Accuracy.', DOI 10.1037/0278-7393.31.6.1267). Candidate 0 (De Bruin et al., 2011, 'Generating keywords improves metacomprehension and self-regulation in elementary and middle school children.', DOI 10.1016/j.jecp.2011.02.005) appears only in general parenthetical '(e.g., ...)' literature lists and for gamma correlation calculation; furthermore, the authors explicitly state in the Limitations section that they did not investigate self-regulation and learning as studied by De Bruin et al. (2011) and instead frame their replication as testing the keyword effect independently of its original proposer K. W. Thiede.
